queue.fact_hook: Octopuses have three hearts and blue copper-based blood; two hearts pump blood through the gills and one pumps it to the body, and the main heart stops beating when they swim.

queue.topic: you could never forget anything
queue.fact_hook: A rare condition called highly superior autobiographical memory has been documented in only a few dozen people, who can recall most days of their lives in detail.

queue.topic: you tried to dig a hole to the other side of the Earth
queue.fact_hook: The deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia, reached about 12,262 meters (7.6 miles) and took nearly 20 years, yet it is only a tiny fraction of the way to Earth's center, and temperatures at the bottom hit around 180°C.

queue.topic: it rained for 40 days straight in your town
queue.fact_hook: Mawsynram in India averages over 11,000 mm (about 467 inches) of rain per year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth, and residents wear woven bamboo-and-leaf rain shields called knups.

queue.topic: you could only eat bananas for a week
queue.fact_hook: Bananas are naturally slightly radioactive because of potassium-40, and the 'banana equivalent dose' is an actual informal unit used to explain radiation levels.

queue.topic: you were a goldfish with a 3-second memory
queue.fact_hook: The 3-second goldfish memory is a myth; experiments have shown goldfish can be trained to respond to signals and remember them for weeks or even months.

queue.topic: you lived in a medieval castle for a day
queue.fact_hook: Medieval castle spiral staircases typically wound clockwise going up, which is commonly said to favor right-handed defenders swinging swords downward against attackers climbing up.

queue.topic: your phone battery lasted a whole year
queue.fact_hook: Most smartphones use lithium-ion batteries, which slowly lose capacity with charge cycles, typically dropping to about 80% after around 500 full charge cycles.

queue.topic: you ate a whole jar of honey in one sitting
queue.fact_hook: Honey never really spoils; edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs thousands of years old, thanks to its low moisture and natural acidity.

queue.topic: you got hiccups that never stopped
queue.fact_hook: Charles Osborne hiccupped for about 68 years, from 1922 to 1990, which is recorded as the longest recorded attack of hiccups.

queue.topic: you tried to outrun a hungry polar bear on thin ice
queue.fact_hook: Polar bear fur is actually transparent and hollow rather than white, and their skin underneath is black, which helps absorb heat.

queue.topic: every clock in the world stopped for a day
queue.fact_hook: GPS satellites carry atomic clocks, and without correcting for relativity effects, GPS positions would drift by roughly 10 kilometers every single day.

queue.topic: you got struck by a snowstorm in the Sahara
queue.fact_hook: Snow has actually fallen in the Sahara Desert; the town of Ain Sefra in Algeria saw snow in 1979, 2016, and again in later years.

queue.topic: you swapped places with a sloth for a day
queue.fact_hook: Sloths only come down from trees about once a week to poop, and their slow metabolism lets algae grow in their fur.

queue.topic: you tried to eat a whole day of food like a Roman gladiator
queue.fact_hook: Analysis of gladiator bones from ancient Ephesus found a diet heavy in barley and beans, and gladiators were nicknamed 'barley men' (hordearii).

queue.topic: you had a cheetah's speed for one day
queue.fact_hook: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to about 100 km/h (60 mph) in roughly three seconds but can only sustain top speed for a few hundred meters.

queue.topic: all the ice cream in the world melted
queue.fact_hook: Ice cream is about half air by volume, an amount called overrun, which is why cheap tubs feel light and why it can be sold by volume.

queue.topic: you tried to hold your breath as long as a sperm whale
queue.fact_hook: Sperm whales can hold their breath for roughly 90 minutes or more while diving over a kilometer deep, storing oxygen mainly in their muscles via myoglobin.

queue.topic: you sneezed with your eyes open
queue.fact_hook: Sneezes can launch droplets at high speed, and while the idea that your eyes would pop out is a myth, closing them is an automatic reflex.

queue.topic: you built a house out of ice like an igloo
queue.fact_hook: Igloos can be much warmer inside than outside; with body heat alone, the interior can be around 0°C to 16°C while outside air is far below freezing, because snow is a good insulator full of trapped air.
